The Times — Friday 25 September 2026, 2.37pm BST. By Fiona Hamilton, Chief Reporter.
[NOTE: published BEFORE the 18:00 Friday cut-off, but the event itself is TOMORROW, Sunday 27 September, so it is forward-looking diary material for the conference opening. Not carried in last night's evening brief.]

HEADLINE: Palestine Action activists to target Andy Burnham's first conference
Standfirst: Campaigners plan to gather in Liverpool to demand that Labour lifts the group's ban, risking arrest under terrorism laws

FACTS:
- Palestine Action activists are planning a mass picketing at Andy Burnham's first party conference as leader, to pressure him over the group's terror ban and Labour's policy on Gaza.
- Campaigners say they will declare their support for Palestine Action, and risk breaking the law, at a protest outside Labour's conference in Liverpool ON SUNDAY (27 September).
- The protest is being planned by Defend Our Juries, a campaign group that has organised events supporting Palestine Action.
- At a meeting this week activists were told to dress in red and hold signs declaring support for Palestine Action, which was banned in July last year. They were advised on tactics to use up police resources including withholding personal details, using burner phones and going "floppy" - becoming a dead weight to make it harder for officers to remove them if arrested.
- Defend Our Juries has told activists to write placards reading "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action", acknowledging it is likely to lead to arrest under the Terrorism Act.
- The High Court ruled in February that Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's decision to ban Palestine Action was unlawful, but that judgment was overturned by the Court of Appeal. A further appeal brought by co-founder Huda Ammori is due to be heard by the SUPREME COURT IN NOVEMBER.
- Gaza is expected to be key at next month's by-election in Camden (Holborn and St Pancras) for Starmer's former seat.
- In July, 28 people were charged with showing support for Palestine Action under the Terrorism Act.

QUOTE (Huda Ammori, Palestine Action co-founder, at the protest briefing): "Palestine Action faces harsher sanctions than Israel." She said Burnham had inherited the issue from Starmer and she wanted to ensure it "isn't just something he's inherited and he can forget about", adding: "It has to be at the forefront of the agenda."

QUOTE (Defend Our Juries action briefing, published online): "Burnham will be looking for ways to distance himself from the previous cabinet. We suggest he starts off strong by deproscribing Palestine Action. The plan is to communicate this to him by sitting outside his first Labour Party conference en masse with our totally peaceful demeanour and signs."
Continuing: "Hundreds of ordinary people getting arrested under terrorism legislation right outside the conference centre windows will show Andy early in his term what the people want and what they will do to get it. He could do the right thing and, as part of a long list, deproscribe Palestine Action now. Or we can be a massive thorn in his side until he does."

QUOTE (Alex Hearn, Labour Against Antisemitism): "These people are so extreme that nothing the government does will ever be enough for them. [Ed] Miliband and Burnham can deproscribe Palestine Action and introduce more and more sanctions to pander to this niche of potential voters, but these far-left activists will still try and destroy the conference."
Continuing: "This latest action isn't protest, it's a strategy to overwhelm the police and maximise disruption. Andy Burnham's first conference as leader is being treated as a target, not a chance to be persuaded. Deproscribing Palestine Action wouldn't be a concession that ends this campaign - it would be seen as further proof that disruption and lawlessness works."

- The Labour Party had been contacted for comment.
